label.en: imperial inquiry whether Wang Xun is well

text.en: When we departed, Xun was well.

translationRepairs: In the winter of the second year of Tianqing (1023), members of the Music Office were all required to wear robes.
In the winter of the second year of Tianqing (1112), members of the Music Office were all required to wear robes.
s0057 dates the Music Office robe rule to 天慶二年冬. Liao Tianqing began in AD 1111 under Tianzuo, so year 2 is AD 1112; the parenthetical 1023 is factually wrong, and 1112 is the correct Western year.
During the Tonghe era (983–1011), the practice was discontinued.
During the Tonghe era (983–1012), the practice was discontinued.
s0026 places the discontinuation 統和中. Tonghe ran thirty years from AD 983 into 1012 (when Kaitai began), so the era span should be 983–1012, not through 1011.
When each has finished awaiting orders, those of low stool rank and above are led forward and asked, 'May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings.'
When each has finished awaiting orders, those of low stool rank and above are led forward and inquire, 'May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings.'
In 可矮墩以上引近前，問「聖躬萬福」, the officials led forward are the agents of 問, greeting the emperor. Passive 'asked' reverses agent and patient; active 'inquire' matches the Chinese and the idiomatic field.

The arrow-verifying officer advances again, takes his place, bows, and announces in full title that the subject reports the imperial arrow verification agrees, then withdraws to stand in the center of the gate.

The arrow-verifying officer advances again, takes his place, bows, and announces in full title that the subject so-and-so reports the imperial arrow verification agrees, then withdraws to stand in the center of the gate.
s0094 has 自通全銜臣某對禦勘箭同; 臣某 is the ritual placeholder 'subject so-and-so'. The before idiomatic drops 某; restoring 'so-and-so' matches the Chinese and the unit's literal.
The Privy Council gate conveys the announcement, "The king inquires whether you are well." The envoys all kneel, and the lead envoy replies, "When we departed, we inquired after his well-being."
The Privy Council gate conveys the announcement, "Is Wang Xun well?" The envoys all kneel, and the lead envoy replies, "When we departed, Xun was well."

閣門傳宣「王詢安否」…大使奏「臣等來時詢安」 uses 王詢 / 詢 as the Goryeo king's personal name in the health-inquiry formula, not the verb 'inquire'. The proposed idiomatic correctly asks whether Wang Xun is well and reports that Xun was well.
The Privy Council gate conveys the announcement, "The king inquires whether you are well"; the envoys all kneel; the lead envoy reports, "When we departed, we inquired after his well-being."
The Privy Council gate conveys the announcement, "Is Wang Xun well?"; the envoys all kneel; the lead envoy reports, "When we departed, Xun was well."
The literal repeats the same misreading of 王詢 and bare 詢 as 'inquire'. Rendering them as the king's name in both the announcement and the reply restores the Chinese sense.
After the Crane Control officers complete obeisance, the usher bows and announces that the King of Goryeo presents tribute with his greetings.
After the Crane Control officers complete obeisance, the usher bows and announces that Wang Xun, King of Goryeo, presents tribute.
通高麗國王詢進奉 announces tribute in the name of King of Goryeo, Xun (Wang Xun). Treating 詢 as 'greetings/inquiry' invents a verb; naming Wang Xun as the tribute presenter is accurate.
When officers of the Crane Control guard complete obeisance, the usher bows and announces the King of Goryeo's inquiry and tribute presentation.
When officers of the Crane Control guard complete obeisance, the usher bows and announces that Wang Xun, King of Goryeo, presents tribute.
The literal likewise misreads 詢 in 高麗國王詢進奉 as 'inquiry'. The proposed wording correctly treats 詢 as the king's given name before 進奉.
